purpose: Test whether candidate lower-level semantic factors can be decomposed into psychophysically measurable or sensorimotor structures rather than merely renamed at a lower layer.
scope_note: This is independent of the open six-concept grounding PR and does not modify linguistic_core@0.3.3 or the living design.

sources.title: Skin and Mechanoreceptor Contribution to Tactile Input for Perception: A Review of Simulation Models
sources.use: Supports treating skin deformation, pressure-related patterns, vibration, and distributed mechanoreceptor activity as measurable inputs to tactile/contact evidence.

sources.title: Assessing proprioception: A critical review of methods
sources.use: Supports treating joint position, movement, and movement discrimination as measurable components of body-configuration estimates.

sources.title: The measurement of proprioceptive accuracy: A systematic literature review
sources.use: Supports measurable subcomponents including joint position, movement, trajectory, velocity, force, muscle tension, weight, and size.

sources.title: Gravity estimation and verticality perception
sources.use: Supports treating gravity-relative orientation as a multisensory estimate combining visual, vestibular, and somatosensory cues rather than a primitive symbolic relation.

sources.title: Features, as well as space and time, guide object persistence
sources.use: Supports treating persistence as constructed from spatiotemporal and feature-based correspondence rather than as an atomic object identity primitive.

sources.title: Staying in bounds: Contextual constraints on object-file coherence
sources.use: Supports the existence of mid-level object-file representations that track entities across time and motion, while leaving the exact grounding algorithm open.

candidate_primitives.label: cutaneous deformation signal
candidate_primitives.note: Local pressure, skin deformation, vibration, and stretch can be psychophysically manipulated and physiologically measured. This is evidence available to a learner; it is not itself a semantic relation.

candidate_primitives.label: proprioceptive configuration signal
candidate_primitives.note: Joint position and movement estimates provide a non-lexical basis for body-part configuration.

candidate_primitives.label: force/load signal
candidate_primitives.note: Force, muscle tension, weight, and pressure are measurable submodalities. They do not by themselves identify support.

candidate_primitives.label: gravity-reference estimate
candidate_primitives.note: Up/down and verticality are modeled as multisensory estimates with measurable bias and precision, not as unexplained symbolic axes.

candidate_primitives.label: spatiotemporal correspondence evidence
candidate_primitives.note: Continuity across position, time, motion, and features provides evidence that successive perceptual episodes belong together; this stops short of assuming a full object identity relation.

candidate_primitives.label: displacement/change signal
candidate_primitives.note: Changes in relative position over time can be measured before assigning semantic labels such as stable, falling, or supported.

audited_factors.construction: A contact hypothesis is licensed when sensory evidence supports coincident boundary interaction, e.g. cutaneous deformation or other cross-modal evidence synchronized with the tracked external pattern.
audited_factors.remaining_gap: Physical contact can occur without conscious tactile evidence and tactile signals can be ambiguous. The semantic factor should therefore represent evidence/estimated contact, not silently equate sensation with metaphysical contact.

audited_factors.construction: Relative-position estimates combine tracked locations/configurations with an explicit reference frame; gravity-relative above/below requires a gravity estimate rather than an ungrounded axis.
audited_factors.remaining_gap: Egocentric, allocentric, object-centered, and gravity-centered reference frames must be represented separately rather than collapsed into one generic spatial relation.

audited_factors.construction: A load-response pattern is a learned covariance between applied force/load evidence, contact/pressure evidence, and observed displacement or stability over time.
audited_factors.remaining_gap: The learner still needs a criterion for the time window and comparison baseline; bounded displacement is not by itself equivalent to support.

audited_factors.construction: Body posture is represented as a learned multimodal configuration over joint/body position, gravity orientation, and contact distribution, without a lexical posture label.
audited_factors.remaining_gap: There is no reason to expect one fixed geometry for categories such as sitting. Category learning must operate over families of variable configurations.

audited_factors.construction: Persistence begins as evidence that successive perceptual episodes form a coherent track under spatiotemporal continuity and feature correspondence.
audited_factors.remaining_gap: A coherent track is not yet a philosophically or ontologically complete identity criterion. Occlusion, replacement, splitting, merging, and indistinguishable duplicates remain adversarial cases.

overall_verdict.summary: The audit does not hit a bottomless renaming regress at these five factors. Each can be pushed into measurable sensory variables or empirically constrained correspondence processes. However, several semantic commitments remain inferential: contact is estimated rather than directly identical with touch, spatial relations require reference frames, persistence still lacks a full identity criterion, and category-level equivalence classes remain learned constructions.
overall_verdict.next_gate: Build a tiny executable measurement-to-factor specimen for one support episode and one posture/persistence episode, with raw observables separated from inferred factors and explicit uncertainty.
